A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 33 pages, including Appendices A-C. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v4 reports original reasoning, in-context learning, and language-modeling experiments in Tables 2-4, plus training/test accuracy analysis in Appendix C and Figure 5.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Tables 2-4 and the training/test accuracy analysis in Appendix C and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The looped architecture, timestep-conditioned scaling, normalization, and training objectives are unchanged. The revised theorem wording clarifies the composition of the existing model without changing its construction.

E1.justification: Both versions use Sudoku, Countdown, longest common subsequence, edit distance, decision-tree in-context learning, and WikiText-103, with the same input lengths and task scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2-4 retain the same standard Transformer and looped Transformer comparisons, including variants with and without timestep encoding. The changed Saunshi citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same data splits, sample counts, loop/depth settings, accuracy/MSE/perplexity metrics, preprocessing, and training configurations.

E4.justification: The loop-count and timestep-encoding comparisons are unchanged. Appendix C.2 and Figure 5 retain the same analysis of training/test accuracy correlation for edit distance; no additional analyses appear.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Tables 2-4 and Figure 5 contain identical results. For example, timestep encoding retains 88.3 accuracy on ED (60) at 100 loops and 22.4 test perplexity on WikiText-103.

T1.justification: v5 inserts N^(1/p) into the sequence-to-token norm bound in Eq. 27 and adds (Nd)^(1/p) multiplying the token/contextual continuity terms in Theorem A.1, Eq. 46. These correct omitted factors; the main Theorem 3.6 bound and underlying constructions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about approximation rates, a limitation of looped architectures, and benefits from timestep encoding. The stated novelty and contribution scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations linking approximation error to weight-tied feed-forward networks, motivating timestep encoding, and using test accuracy as an approximation proxy are retained. Applicability qualifications and future-work directions are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains the same data-generation algorithm, model dimensions, optimizer settings, initialization, training budgets, and loss details. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The Saunshi et al. reference changes from the 2024 paper 'On the inductive bias of stacking towards improving reasoning' to the 2025 paper 'Reasoning with latent thoughts: On the power of looped transformers.' Section 2.2 also adds the latter citation for multilayer implementations. Broader research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized wording, capitalization, and grammatical edits, including clearer descriptions of the model composition in Theorems 3.6 and A.1. Section order and the overall narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v5 removes the first-page proceedings/copyright footer and slightly reflows text, definitions, and equations. All figures and tables retain their content, structure, and placement; the layout changes are limited.

improvement.justification: Correcting Eq. 27 and Theorem A.1's missing factors improves mathematical accuracy and aligns the appendix theorem statement with the existing bound in Eq. 109 and Theorem 3.6. The gain is limited: the analogous appendix Eq. 104 still omits N^(1/p), while the method, experimental evidence, and central claims remain unchanged.
